block.comment: Purpose: Map a potentiometer to servo pulse microseconds for finer command increments than whole degree values. Wiring: Servo: PIN D9; analog read: PIN A0; Potentiometer outer legs VCC/GND; wiper on the listed analog input. Common GND; use each module’s required supply. Try: Turn A0 and adjust the minimum/maximum pulse widths to your servo’s usable travel.
Measure the voltage on this analog input. On ATmega168/328, the ADC returns 0–1023; other boards may use a different ADC range. A potentiometer wiper or analog sensor connects here.
Convert a value from one numeric range to another. All five inputs can be expressions. Arduino map uses integer arithmetic and does not clamp values outside the source range.
Wait for the given number of milliseconds (1000 ms = 1 second). This pauses the main program; avoid long waits when loop must service motors, music files or serial input.
Send a target position to the named servo. The library keeps generating pulses; reaching the target takes mechanical time. Position mode uses degrees, pulse mode uses microseconds.
